services.name: Root canal treatment
services.short: Save a painful or infected tooth instead of losing it.
services.lede: Root canal treatment removes the inflamed or infected pulp from inside a tooth, cleans and seals the canals, and lets you keep a tooth that would otherwise need to come out.
services.visits: Usually one to three visits, depending on the tooth and how much infection there is.
signs: Pain with hot or cold that lingers after the drink is gone
Pain when biting or chewing on one tooth
Throbbing toothache that wakes you at night
A swollen gum or a pimple-like bump near a tooth
A tooth that has darkened after a knock or injury
A very deep cavity or a broken tooth that reaches the nerve
after: Some tenderness for a few days is normal; it settles on its own or with ordinary pain relief.
Avoid chewing hard food on the tooth until the final crown or filling is in place.
Brush and floss normally.
Call us if swelling increases, pain gets worse instead of better, or the temporary filling falls out.
faqs: Does root canal treatment hurt?
It is done under local anaesthetic, so it should feel much like having a filling. Most people come in with pain and leave with less of it.
Why do I need a crown afterwards?
A treated back tooth has lost much of its inner structure and can crack under chewing forces. A crown holds it together. We will tell you whether your tooth needs one.
Is it better to just pull the tooth out?

Keeping your natural tooth is usually the better choice when it can be restored. A gap lets neighbouring teeth drift and then needs an implant, bridge or denture to fill it. We will explain both options and what each involves.
How long will the tooth last?
With a good final restoration and normal brushing, flossing and check-ups, a root-canal-treated tooth can last for many years.
services.urgent: Facial swelling that is spreading, fever, or difficulty swallowing or breathing needs urgent attention: call us straight away, or go to a hospital emergency department.

services.name: Dental implants
services.short: A fixed, long-term replacement for one or more missing teeth.
services.lede: A dental implant is a small titanium post placed in the jawbone where a tooth root used to be. Once it has bonded with the bone, a crown is fixed on top. It does not rely on the neighbouring teeth for support.
services.visits: Several visits spread over a few months, mostly because of the healing time.
signs: You have one or more missing teeth
You want a fixed tooth rather than one you remove
Your gums are healthy, or can be treated first
There is enough jawbone to hold the implant, or it can be built up
You want to stabilise a loose denture
after: Expect some swelling and tenderness for a few days after placement.
Stick to soft food on that side at first, and do not smoke.
Clean around the implant as carefully as a natural tooth: brushing, and floss or interdental brushes.
Keep your regular check-ups; gum disease can affect implants too.
faqs: How long does the whole process take?
Usually several months from placement to the final crown, mostly waiting for the bone to heal around the implant. Your plan will give you a realistic timeline.
Am I too old for an implant?
Age alone is rarely the barrier. General health, gum health and the amount of bone matter more.
Implant or bridge: which is better?
An implant does not need the neighbouring teeth to be cut down, while a bridge is quicker and does not involve surgery. We will go through both for your situation.
Can implants hold a denture in place?
Yes. A small number of implants can be used to anchor a denture so it does not move when you eat or speak.
services.urgent: Bleeding that will not stop with firm pressure, or swelling and pain that keep getting worse after the first few days, are reasons to call us.

services.name: Crowns & bridges
services.short: Metal-ceramic and zirconia crowns, and fixed bridges for missing teeth.
services.lede: A crown is a cap that covers the whole visible part of a tooth to protect and restore it. A bridge, also called a fixed partial denture, replaces a missing tooth by anchoring a false tooth to crowns on the teeth either side.
signs: A back tooth has had root canal treatment
A tooth is cracked, heavily filled or badly worn
A large filling keeps breaking
A tooth is discoloured or misshapen and a filling will not do
You have a gap from a missing tooth with healthy teeth on either side
after: Your bite may feel different for a day or two. If it still feels high, come back for a quick adjustment.
Brush and floss as normal. Under a bridge, use a floss threader or interdental brush to clean the gap.
Avoid using your teeth to open packets or bite very hard objects.
faqs: Does preparing a tooth for a crown hurt?
It is done under local anaesthetic. The tooth can be a little sensitive for a few days afterwards.
How do I clean under a bridge?
Food collects under the false tooth, so thread floss or a small interdental brush under it every day. We will show you how.
Can a crown be whitened later?
No. Whitening does not change the colour of crowns, so if you want whiter teeth, whiten first and match the crown afterwards.
choices: Porcelain fused over a metal base. Strong and long-established. Over time a thin dark line can sometimes show at the gum.
Metal-free and tooth-coloured all the way through, and very strong. A popular choice where appearance matters.

services.name: Dentures
services.short: Removable partial dentures and complete dentures.
services.lede: Dentures are removable replacements for missing teeth. A removable partial denture (RPD) fills gaps when some natural teeth remain; a complete denture replaces all the teeth in an upper or lower jaw.
services.visits: Several visits over a few weeks.
signs: You have lost several teeth and want to chew and smile comfortably again
You have no teeth left in one or both jaws
You need a replacement that is less invasive than implants
Your current denture is loose, cracked or uncomfortable
after: Speaking and eating take practice. Start with soft food cut into small pieces.
Sore spots are common at first. Come back so we can adjust the denture; do not put up with them.
Take the denture out and clean it every day, and rinse it after meals.
Clean it over a basin of water or a folded towel so it does not break if dropped.
Never use hot water, which can warp it.
faqs: How long does it take to get used to dentures?
It varies, but most people adapt to speaking and eating over a few weeks.
Should I sleep with my dentures in?
Generally it is advised to take them out at night to rest the gums. We will tell you what is right in your case.
Why does my old denture feel loose?
The gums and bone change shape over time, so a denture that once fitted can become loose. It may need relining or replacing.
Can a loose denture be made more stable?
Yes, dental implants can be used to anchor a denture. Ask about it at your visit.

services.name: Scaling & gum treatment
services.short: Cleaning above and below the gum line, root planing and gum care.
services.lede: Tartar is hardened plaque that brushing cannot remove. Scaling cleans it off the teeth, both above the gum line (supra-gingival) and below it (sub-gingival). Where gum disease has created deeper pockets, root planing smooths the root surfaces so the gums can heal.
services.visits: A routine scaling is usually a single visit. Deeper gum treatment can take more.
signs: Gums that bleed when you brush or floss
Red, swollen or tender gums
Bad breath that does not go away
Gums pulling back so the teeth look longer
Teeth that feel loose or are moving
Hard yellow or brown deposits along the gum line
after: Teeth can feel sensitive for a few days.
Some bleeding when brushing in the first days is normal and should reduce as the gums heal.
Brush twice a day and clean between your teeth daily to stop tartar building up again.
faqs: Does scaling damage the enamel or loosen teeth?

No. Scaling removes deposits from the tooth surface; done properly it does not weaken enamel. Teeth can feel slightly loose or gaps can look bigger afterwards because tartar was filling those spaces, not because scaling caused damage.
How often do I need scaling?
It depends on how quickly tartar builds up for you and the health of your gums. We will recommend an interval after your examination.
Why do my gums bleed after scaling?
Inflamed gums bleed easily. As the inflammation settles after cleaning, bleeding usually reduces over the following weeks.

services.name: Tooth extraction
services.short: Simple extractions and impacted wisdom teeth.
services.lede: We always try to save a tooth first. When that is not possible, removing it gently and caring for the socket properly makes recovery much easier.
services.visits: Usually a single visit, with a review if stitches were placed.
signs: It is too broken or decayed to be restored
Gum disease has left it very loose
A wisdom tooth is impacted and causing pain, swelling or infection
It is needed for orthodontic treatment
after: Keep firm pressure on the gauze for the time we advise.
For the first 24 hours, do not rinse vigorously, spit forcefully or use a straw. These can dislodge the clot.
Do not smoke.
Eat soft, cool food and chew on the other side.
After the first day, gentle warm salt-water rinses help keep the area clean.
Severe pain that starts a few days later can mean a dry socket. Come back so we can treat it.
faqs: Do all wisdom teeth need to be removed?
No. Wisdom teeth that are healthy and causing no problems can usually stay. We advise removal when one is causing pain, infection or damage to the next tooth.
I take blood thinners or have diabetes. Can I still have a tooth out?
Usually yes, with planning. Tell us about every medicine and condition beforehand, and do not stop any medicine without your doctor’s advice.
What can replace the tooth afterwards?
An implant, a bridge or a partial denture. We can talk through the options before the extraction.
services.urgent: Bleeding that will not stop after an hour of firm pressure, swelling that keeps increasing, or fever: call us straight away.

services.name: Orthodontics
services.short: Straighter teeth, closed gaps and a better bite.
services.lede: Orthodontic treatment moves teeth into better positions, using gentle, steady pressure over time. It can straighten crowded teeth, close gaps and improve how the teeth bite together.
services.visits: Treatment usually runs for months to a couple of years, with regular adjustment visits.
signs: Crowded or overlapping teeth
Gaps between teeth
Front teeth that stick out
A bite where upper and lower teeth do not meet properly
Teeth that are hard to clean because of their position
after: Teeth often feel sore for a few days after fitting or an adjustment.
Cleaning takes extra care. We will show you how to brush and clean around the appliance.
Avoid very hard or sticky food that can break braces.
Wear your retainer exactly as advised. Without it, teeth tend to drift back.
faqs: Am I too old for braces?
No. Adults can have orthodontic treatment as long as the teeth and gums are healthy.
How long does treatment take?
It depends on how much the teeth need to move. Many cases take from several months to two years. Your plan will give an estimate.
Why do I need a retainer?
Teeth naturally try to move back towards their old positions. A retainer keeps the result.

services.name: Fillings & whitening
services.short: Tooth-coloured fillings, deep cavity care and teeth whitening.
services.lede: Most cavities can be repaired with a tooth-coloured filling in a single visit. If your teeth are healthy but stained, professional whitening can lighten their natural colour.
services.visits: A filling is usually done in one visit.
signs: A tooth is sensitive to sweet, hot or cold
Food keeps getting stuck in one spot
You can see or feel a hole or a dark area
An old filling is broken or has a gap around it
after: Wait until the numbness wears off before eating, so you do not bite your cheek or lip.
Mild sensitivity after a deep filling can last a little while. If it gets worse, or you get throbbing pain, call us.
After whitening, temporary sensitivity is common. Tea, coffee and tobacco will stain the teeth again over time.
faqs: Will whitening change the colour of my crowns or fillings?
No. Whitening only works on natural teeth, so existing crowns and fillings may need replacing to match afterwards.
Is whitening safe?
When done under a dentist’s supervision after a check-up, whitening is generally safe. Temporary sensitivity is the most common side effect.
How long does a filling last?
That depends on its size, where it is and how well the tooth is cared for. Regular check-ups let us spot a failing filling early.
choices: Decay is removed and the tooth is rebuilt with a tooth-coloured composite. When a cavity is very deep and close to the nerve, the aim is to protect the pulp and keep the tooth alive. If the nerve is already damaged, root canal treatment may be needed.
Whitening lightens the natural colour of your teeth under a dentist’s supervision. We check your teeth and gums first, because cavities and gum problems should be treated before whitening.

faqs: What are your opening hours?
We are open 7:30 AM – 7:30 PM, every day.
Where is the clinic?
At Tenzing Chowk in Kapan, Kathmandu. See the contact page for a map.
How do I book an appointment?
Call us, send a WhatsApp message, or fill in the appointment request form and we will call you back to confirm a time.
Which treatments do you offer?
General and preventive care, fillings, root canal treatment, crowns and bridges, dentures, implants, gum treatment, extractions including wisdom teeth, orthodontics and whitening, all in one clinic.
